A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same pop-up attack study. All 14 pages of each version, including tables, figures and Appendix A, support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack evaluations on OSWorld and VisualWebArena, including model comparisons, ablations, defense experiments and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendix, including the relocated step-wise defense experiment.

M1.justification: The four-part pop-up attack, query summarization/speculation, placement procedure and attack variants are unchanged. Removing 'Please click' was already tested in v1 Appendix A; its appearance in v2 Section 4.3 introduces no new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate OSWorld screenshot and SoM agents and VisualWebArena SoM agents. The same task coverage, pop-up scenarios and delayed-onset attacks are retained.

E2.justification: The same five VLM backbones and the same defense and attack-variant comparisons remain. 'System Prompt Defense' and '+ Attack Variance' relabel existing comparisons rather than add comparators.

E3.justification: The 50 OSWorld tasks, 72 VisualWebArena tasks, decoding settings and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. The 15- and 30-step limits now stated in Section 4 were already documented in v1 Figure 3. The relocated defense experiment retains its protocol.

E4.justification: The component ablations, blank/small pop-up tests, thought annotations, failure cases and delayed-attack analyses are retained. The step-wise defense and instruction-removal experiment moves from v1 Appendix A, Table 10, to v2 Section 4.3, Table 8, without new evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point estimates and task/step distributions. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: The matched tables and result graphics retain their numerical values and findings. In particular, v1 Table 10 and v2 Table 8 both report step-wise-defense ASRs of 5.9% and 10.4%, with TASRs of 32% and 44%.

T1.justification: The threat-model assumptions and metric definitions are unchanged. Neither version contains added or revised theorems, proofs or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: v2 narrows the introduction's claim about ineffective prompt defenses to instructions placed in system prompts. The central vulnerability claim and headline 86% attack success rate and 47% task-success decrease remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds the hypothesis that emphasizing safety in prompts may impair planning and grounding, explaining limited task-success recovery despite reduced attack success. This interpretation is new, but no new analysis tests it; the other mechanism explanations and limitations largely persist.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-repository link in the abstract. Existing prompts, model identifiers, placement rules and size limits are retained; moving implementation prose into Appendix A does not establish an implementation change.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to InjecAgent, UI-TARS, Aguvis, Collaborative Gym and OpenAI's agent-building guide. These update the discussion of attacks, future agents, human oversight and defenses without substantially changing the research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 consolidates defense material in Section 4.3, moves placement details into Appendix A, and adds an Ethical Considerations section. Local wording and terminology are refined, while the overall section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with adjusted spacing and typography. Tables and captions become more compact, some figures are resized or repositioned, and the step-wise defense table moves into the main text with corresponding table renumbering. No result display is substantively added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 gives the existing step-wise defense results greater prominence and qualifies the introduction's defense claim, improving balance and clarity. The code-access pointer also improves reproducibility documentation. These are limited gains: the empirical evidence is unchanged, and the added planning/grounding explanation remains a hypothesis.
